rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Results, Table 1 - the authors train AlexNet and GoogLeNet on 54,306 PlantVillage leaf images across 60 experimental configurations and report mean F1 scores and accuracies (best 99.35% on held-out test set; ~31% on external online images).
rows.notes: The study classifies individual, detached leaf photographs taken under controlled conditions (and a small set of online images) into 38 crop-disease classes. It is not remote sensing or UAV imagery, and it does not grade infection severity, detect disease before canopy-wide symptoms, or test any targeted response or control action. It supports only the upstream step (image-based disease identification) with a different image technology. The Discussion itself states the model is constrained to single leaves on homogeneous backgrounds and that accuracy drops to ~31% on images from other conditions, and that early-stage visual diagnosis is challenging.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a leaf-image deep-learning classification benchmark (PlantVillage), not a remote-sensing or pest-control study.
